blocking_findings.title: C2 accepts unrelated denials even when the merge ran
blocking_findings.finding: The required merge-refusal check treats any denied tool input containing the substring gh pr merge as proof. It neither checks tool_name nor requires the attempted CMD, and exits 0 before inspecting evidence that execution occurred. Controlled subprocess responses demonstrated PASS for an unrelated denied Bash echo and a denied Read pathname while result explicitly said Could not resolve to a PullRequest. donectl.verify converts this exit 0 into PROVEN, so C2 can certify a failed guard. This finding concerns the acceptance test, not a demonstrated bypass of the deny rule.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Executed the unchanged script using runpy.run_path with subprocess.run patched to CompletedProcess([], 0, json.dumps({"permission_denials":[{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo 'gh pr merge'"}}],"result":"Could not resolve to a PullRequest"}), ""). Observed SystemExit(0) and PASS. Replacing that denial with tool_name=Read and file_path=/tmp/gh pr merge notes also returned 0. Positive control with no denial and the same result returned 1; no tool evidence returned 2. No real merge or model request was executed.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Require a Bash denial for the exact requested command; reject contradictory execution evidence before accepting a denial. Prefer structured tool execution evidence over narrative output. Add negative fixtures for unrelated denials and mixed executed/denied attempts, then re-run the real rule-present/rule-removed control.

attack_evidence: Removed the added deny rule: C1 and C3 both failed (exit 1); restored settings byte-identical.
Changed attribution.sessionUrl, added an unrelated root key, changed permissions.allow, and removed an existing deny entry: C3 rejected each. Therefore tested other-key changes do not evade C3.
Duplicated an existing deny entry: C3 returned PASS, demonstrating a multiplicity blind spot; documented as nonblocking because duplicate rules do not change deny semantics.

Injected unrelated Bash echo and Read permission denials alongside explicit command-executed output: unchanged C2 returned PASS in both cases. A matching denial plus an earlier execution report also returned PASS.
The requested --auto, --squash-before-number and leading-cd forms were not verified in a live Claude session. No synthetic matcher was substituted for Claude enforcement.
